chunks: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “One day, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was sitting with Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah when he said to him: ‘O Muḥammad, bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer).’”

So Muḥammad brought him the water, and he poured with his right hand onto his left hand, then said: “In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and all praise belongs to Allah, who made water purifying and did not make it impure.”
He said: “Then he performed istinjāʾ and said: ‘O Allah, protect my private part and keep it chaste, cover my nakedness, and make me forbidden to the Fire.’”
He said: “Then he rinsed his mouth and said: ‘O Allah, prompt me with my proof on the day I meet You, and loosen my tongue with Your dhikr and Your shukr.’”
Then he sniffed water into his nose and said: “O Allah, do not forbid me the fragrance of Jannah, and make me among those who smell its fragrance, its gentle breeze, and its perfume.”
He said: “Then he washed his face and said: ‘O Allah, brighten my face on the day when faces will be darkened, and do not darken my face on the day when faces will be brightened.’”
Then he washed his right hand and said: “O Allah, give me my book in my right hand, and everlasting life in the gardens in my left, and reckon me with an easy reckoning.”

Then he washed his left hand and said: “O Allah, do not give me my book in my left hand, and do not make it shackled to my neck, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from the severing torments of the fires.”
Then he wiped his head and said: “O Allah, envelop me in Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your pardon.”
Then he wiped his feet and said: “O Allah, make me steadfast upon the ṣirāṭ on the day when feet will slip, and make my striving in that which pleases You with me, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.”

Then he raised his head and looked at Muḥammad and said: “O Muḥammad, whoever performs wudu (ablution) like my wudu and says the like of what I say, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, creates from every drop an angel that sanctifies Him, glorifies Him, and magnifies Him; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes the reward of that for him until the Day of Qiyamah.”

key_terms.اسْتَنْجَى: he performed cleansing of the private area
key_terms.اسْتَنْشَقَ: he drew water into the nose in wudu
key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ: the path over which steadfastness is sought on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water as the means of ritual purification
key_terms.تَمَضْمَضَ: he rinsed the mouth in wudu

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام recite during each step of wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the wudu (ablution) of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام together with the supplications recited at each step. It combines ritual purification with du'a (supplication), remembrance of Allah, and awareness of the afterlife, ending with the promise of great reward for one who performs wudu in this manner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.84 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"One day, The Commander of the Faithful (as) was sitting with Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah when He said to him: 'O’ Muhammad, bring me a container of water so I can perform wudu for prayer.'
Muhammad brought him the water, and he poured it with his right hand onto his left hand, then said:
Bismillāhi wa billāhi wal-ḥamdu lillāhi alladhī ja‘ala al-mā’a ṭahūran wa lam
yaj‘alhu najisan
'In the name of Allah (swt) and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt) who made water purifying and did not make it impure.'
He then performed istinja and said:
Allāhumma ḥaṣṣin farjī wa a‘iffahu wa ustur ‘awratī wa ḥarrimnī ‘ala al-nār
'O’ Allah (swt), protect my private part and keep it chaste; cover my private areas and forbid me from the Fire.'.
Then He rinsed his mouth and said:
Allāhumma laqqinnī ḥujjatī yawma alqāk wa aṭliq lisānī bidhikrika
wa shukrika
'O’ Allah (swt), grant me the ability to present my arguments on the Day I meet You, and loosen my tongue to remember You and to thank You.'.
He then sniffed water and said:
Allāhumma lā tuḥarrim ‘alayya rīḥa al-jannah wa aj‘alnī mimman yashammu rīḥahā wa rawḥahā wa ṭībahā
'O’ Allah (swt), do not make me forbidden from the fragrance of Paradise, and make me among those who can smell its scent and enjoy its sweetness.'.
He washed his face and said:
Allāhumma bayyiḍ wajhī yawma taswaddu fīhi al-wujūh wa lā tusawwid wajhī yawma tabyaḍḍu fīhi al-wujūh
'O’ Allah (swt), make my face white on the Day when faces are darkened, and do not make my face dark on the Day when faces are made luminous.'.
He then washed his right hand and said:
Allāhumma a‘ṭinī kitābī biyamīnī wa al-khuld fī al-jinān biyasārī wa ḥāsibnī ḥisāban yasīran
'O’ Allah (swt), grant me my book in my right hand and grant me eternity in Paradise with my left hand, and hold me accountable with an easy account.'
He then washed his left hand and said:
Allāhumma lā tu‘ṭinī kitābī biyasārī wa lā taj‘alhā maghlūlatan ilā ‘unuqī wa a‘ūdhu bika rabbī min muqaṭṭa‘āti al-nīrān
'O’ Allah (swt), do not grant me my book in my left hand, and do not make it tied around my neck. I seek refuge in You, O’ my Lord (azj), from the torments of the Fire.'
He then wiped his head and said:
Allāhumma ghshshinī biraḥmatika wa barakātika wa ‘afwika
'O’ Allah (swt), envelop me in Your mercy, blessings, and forgiveness.'
He then wiped his feet and said:
Allāhumma thabbitnī ‘ala al-ṣirāṭ yawma tazillu fīhi al-aqdām wa aj‘al sa‘yī fīmā yurḍīka ‘annī yā dhā al-jalāli wa al-ikrām
'O’ Allah (swt), keep me steadfast on the Straight Path on the Day when the feet may slip, and make my efforts pleasing to You, O’ Lord (azj) of Glory and Honor.'
He then raised his head and looked at Muhammad and said:
'O’ Muhammad, whoever performs wudu like my wudu and recites like my recitations, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, will create an angel from every drop [of water] that purifies him, and that angel will glorify and praise Allah (swt), and Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, will record the reward for him until the Day of Resurrection.'".
